why_they_differ: The four numbers 80, 81, 84, 85 are NOT invalid on the 138C .fse -- each occurs, exactly once, at (54, 88), (54, 89), (54, 92), (54, 93) -- so `chipdb.py`'s existing linear search (which stops at the first match) already resolves to a real, unique cell for every one of the four types, on both devices. What differs is the geometry those four cells sit in. On GW5A-25A (37x92 grid, single clock plane) the same four types cluster at the single geometric center row (row 18 = floor(37/2), columns 43/44/47/48, i.e. two adjacent pairs either side of center_col) and that one cluster is provably sufficient, because 25A has one clock plane. On GW5AST-138C (109x182 grid) the four types cluster the same way -- one row (54 = floor(109/2)), four adjacent columns (88/89/92/93) either side of center_col -- but P1.T04 already measured 138C as a two-half topology (top half rows ~0-53, bottom half rows ~54-108, joined by a central bridge, 6 HCLK blocks split 2-top/4-bottom, not a single plane). A single central-row cluster of 4 types can only be the right host for a two-half device if the same 4 physical cells are genuinely shared/muxed between both halves -- an assumption the pre-5A-derived search never had to make and was never verified for 138C. The 8-run oracle probe below (fuzz.gw5ast138c.shapes.clocking_dqce_probe, sequences A/B, n_dqce=1..4) answers that empirically by testing whether the vendor toolchain's own DCE placements (see naming note) land inside this same 4-cell cluster or elsewhere.
naming_note: MEASURED (this task): the vendor Verilog primitive for Dynamic Clock Enable on the Arora V / GW5A(ST) family is named `DCE`, not `DQCE` -- `DQCE` does not appear anywhere in UG306-1.0.1E (Arora V Clock User Guide; DCE is S3.1, port-identical to DQCE: CLKIN/CE/CLKOUT). Compiling `examples/dqce.v`'s generic (pre-5A) `DQCE` instantiation against GW5AST-138C fails at Gowin's own Verilog elaboration with `EX3937 Instantiating unknown module 'DQCE'`; renaming the instantiated module to `DCE` (same ports) compiles cleanly. apycula's own chipdb.py `extra_func['dqce']` key is an internal dict name unaffected by this -- it is not itself the vendor's instantiable Verilog identifier -- but any GW5A(ST)-targeted design (this probe, or a future user-facing example) must instantiate `DCE`, and this is worth carrying to whichever task authors a GW5A DQCE/DCE user example.

measured_placement.method: presence_diff(baseline=oracle-smoke/top.fs, instance=A4.fs|B4.fs) -- A4/B4 are the n_dqce=4 builds of each CE sequence (8-run batch, p1-dqce-types), reusing the kept .fs from the 8 successful oracle compiles (all verdict=ok, 0 aborted).

81@(54,89).status: ASSUMED -- 0 fuse bits moved in either build; a 4-instance test does not rule this cell out (apycula's own model gives each quadrant cell 6 dqce[j] sub-slots, `chipdb.py:2895-2911`, so 4 combinational-CE instances may simply not have needed a 4th distinct physical host). Confirming or refuting 81@(54,89) as a real DCE host needs >=6 simultaneous, spine-distinct instances -- out of this task's 8-run budget; left for P1.T29/T30 (which build the real 24-instance, 4-quadrant design anyway).
